name: og-06-chemistry-to-heredity
title: The First Heredity
question: Does inherited state improve persistence/throughput — comparing RNA-like, peptide-assisted, compositional and hybrid heredity — rather than template replication in isolation? (Do NOT presume RNA.)
hypothesis: At least one heredity module raises lineage persistence + information retention above its non-heritable control under a feasible resource budget; the winner is not assumed a priori.
objective: Introduce competing heredity modules and test whether inherited state improves persistence under feasible budgets.
proposed_mechanisms: J: polymers, information and heredity (as competing modules)

conditions.name: reproducibility
conditions.expr: solver and db and seed and scenario recorded

contract.note: bigraph-schema typed ports (_type/_units/bounds) + conservation predicates; the composite built for this study must declare a ProcessContract matching this face (audited via the workbench §Contract panel).

behavior_tests.name: inheritance-beats-noninheritance
behavior_tests.description: The RNA-like heredity module retains functional information and outscores the non-heritable control (whose function degrades away).

measure.detail: RNA-like lineage fitness at steady state

pass_if.detail: inheriting lineage fitness net-positive (and beats the non-heritable control)

behavior_tests.name: information-retained-above-error-threshold
behavior_tests.description: The RNA-like module sits above the Eigen error threshold — functional information is retained (C/(C+E) high), not lost to the error catastrophe.

pass_if.detail: functional information retained (above the error threshold)

behavior_tests.name: heredity-modules-compared
behavior_tests.description: Two viable heredity modules compared head-to-head: RNA-like (long, high-fidelity) outscores the cheaper, lower-fidelity peptide module — an evidence-based ranking, not assumed.

pass_if.detail: both modules viable; RNA-like ranks above peptide

behavior_tests.name: error-catastrophe-below-threshold
behavior_tests.description: Discriminating (Eigen): below the error threshold (low fidelity × long sequence) functional information is lost — retention collapses and inheritance fails.

behavior_tests.name: replication-feasible-budget
behavior_tests.description: Inheritance pays within a feasible replication budget — net-positive fitness after the replication cost, not idealized.

behavior_tests.name: heredity-lineage-compositional-persists
behavior_tests.description: Do NOT presume RNA. In the agent-based lineage model, compositional (GARD) heredity retains functional information across generations — length-independent — above the non-heritable control, so heredity need not be a long high-fidelity template.

measure.detail: compositional vs non-heritable functional persistence in the agent-based lineage

pass_if.detail: compositional persistence above threshold and above the non-heritable control (realized heritability separates them)

literature_anchors.expectation: Mineral/CO-driven peptide formation at 100 C, pH 7-10
literature_anchors.status_in_workspace: Represented as the peptide heredity arm in the agent-based lineage comparison (graded fitness 0.24, below RNA-like 0.38 and the compositional/hybrid arms); a reduced coupling, not a first-principles peptide-formation-rate reproduction

claim: An inherited chemical state improves lineage fitness above its replication cost when it clears the Eigen error threshold — but heredity need NOT presume a long high-fidelity RNA template. An agent-based lineage shows template heredity suffers the length catastrophe (Q=fidelity^length collapses with length) while compositional (GARD) and template-focused hybrid heredity persist length-independently (functional persistence ~0.88, seed-robust across the 5 graded seeds — 0.878±0.005, and 8/8 in a wider sweep) above the non-heritable control, which loses the parent↔offspring correlation and collapses. (A mean-field quasispecies arm still ranks a long high-fidelity template above a cheaper peptide module above non-inheritance when all clear the threshold.)

findings.statement: A high-fidelity heredity module (RNA-like, 30-mer, per-site fidelity 0.99 → whole-sequence Q=0.74) retains functional information (C/(C+E)=0.62) and achieves net-positive lineage fitness (0.38) after its replication cost, outscoring the non-heritable control whose function degrades away.
findings.explanation: Real libRoadRunner quasispecies ODE; above the Eigen error threshold correct templates outreplicate the mutational error tail (Eigen 1971).

findings.statement: Heredity modules rank by an evidence-based head-to-head — RNA-like (0.38) beats the cheaper, lower-fidelity peptide module (0.24), and both beat non-inheritance — while a module below the error threshold (per-site 0.90 × 30-mer, Q=0.04) suffers the error catastrophe (retention 0, fitness −0.10).
findings.explanation: Whole-sequence fidelity Q = per_site_fidelity^length sets the threshold; longer high-fidelity polymers retain more information but cost more to replicate.

findings.statement: An agent-based LINEAGE model (individuals inherit a chemical phenotype at fission into a real tree) reproduces the Eigen error threshold (the imposed Q=fidelity^length relation) as a functional-persistence boundary in (per-site fidelity × length) space — AND shows that heredity need not presume a long high-fidelity template — compositional (GARD) and template-focused hybrid heredity persist at functional-persistence ~0.88 (seed-robust — 0.878±0.005 across the 5 graded seeds, 8/8 in a wider sweep) INDEPENDENT of length, where a long low-fidelity template collapses; the non-heritable control loses the parent↔offspring correlation (realized heritability ~0.04–0.11 vs 0.92–0.99 for the heritable modules) and crashes to ~5 individuals.

evidence.observed: compositional persistence 0.878±0.005 across 5 graded seeds (heritability 0.92), hybrid ~0.88 (0.92) — length-independent; template needs Q=fidelity^length above threshold; non-heritable heritability ~0.04–0.11, collapses every seed

findings.explanation: Coarse-grained agent-based reproduction with explicit fidelity/cost/competition. Template inheritance ratchets (Eigen 1971, no back-mutation) so a long low-fidelity template loses information; compositional inheritance drifts by multinomial fission of an autocatalytic composition (GARD, Segré 2000) — length-independent, so it escapes the length catastrophe. The realized heritability (offspring↔parent φ slope) separates true inheritance from the non-heritable control.

biological_validation.basis: Reproduces the Eigen error threshold (inheritance pays above it, collapses below it) at both mean-field and individual-lineage level, ranks viable modules head-to-head, and shows non-template (compositional/hybrid) heredity persisting length-independently.

explanatory_gain.basis: Two independent engines — a quasispecies ODE and an agent-based lineage — both reproduce the consequences of the fidelity × length error threshold (the imposed Q=fidelity^length relation) — collapse above the length catastrophe, escape for non-template modes — and the lineage additionally shows compositional/hybrid heredity escaping the length catastrophe (heredity need not presume RNA).

limitations: The functional benefit and replication cost are reduced couplings; the quasispecies ODE and the agent-based lineage are the real engines.
The mean-field arm compares two modules (RNA-like, peptide); the agent-based lineage compares four (template, compositional, hybrid, non-heritable). A fuller chemical module library is deferred.

resolved_uncertainties: Inheritance improves fitness above the Eigen error threshold and can be ranked across modules by an evidence-based head-to-head.
Heredity need not presume a long high-fidelity RNA template — compositional (GARD) and hybrid heredity persist length-independently above the non-heritable control.
remaining_uncertainties: Whether an inherited catalyst actually raises the og-02 network's metabolic throughput in-lineage.

followup_study_proposals.rationale: Couple the winning heredity module to the og-02 rTCA network; measure inherited-catalyst throughput gain.

key_assumptions: Treat informational chemistry as a branch point; do not presume a viable RNA replication mechanism.
expert_questions: Which heredity modules to prioritize first: RNA-world, peptide-first, compositional, or mineral-surface templating?

conclusion: Two real engines agree. A libRoadRunner quasispecies ODE shows inheritance is favored above the Eigen error threshold and ranks modules head-to-head; an agent-based lineage (individuals dividing into a phenotype tree) reproduces that threshold AND shows that compositional/hybrid heredity escapes the length catastrophe — so the heredity transition does not require a long high-fidelity RNA template. Opens the genetic era of the campaign (og-07 ecology, og-08 escape).
